gui.mcjavasafetycheck.main.title: %s: Java Safety Check
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.main.body: %s checked the Java this game runs on. It has Java4Shell, a publicly reported flaw that a hostile multiplayer server could use to run code on your computer. Fixing it is free and takes a minute.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.main.trust: Checked on this PC only. Nothing was sent anywhere. %s will never ask for passwords or payment.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.update.title: Update Java
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.update.how.minecra: Your Java comes from the Minecraft Launcher, which updates it for you. Close the launcher completely and open it again to get the newest Java.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.update.how.cursefo: Your Java comes from the CurseForge app, which updates it for you. Close CurseForge completely and open it again to get the newest Java.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.update.how.atlaunc: Your Java comes from ATLauncher, which updates it for you. Close ATLauncher completely and open it again to get the newest Java.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.update.how.modrint: Your Java was downloaded by the Modrinth App. Open its Settings, go to Java installations and press Install recommended next to Java %s. Then restart the game.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.update.how.prism: Your Java was downloaded by Prism Launcher. Open Settings > Java, choose Download Java and pick the newest Java %s. Select it, then restart the game.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.update.how.own: You installed this Java yourself (%1$s). Download the newest Java %2$s from %1$s, install it, and make sure your launcher uses it.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.update.note: Fixed Java builds are still rolling out. If yours isn't out yet, use the arguments instead.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.args.title: Use Arguments
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.args.body: Add this to your launcher's JVM arguments, then restart the game. It switches off only the faulty part of Java.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.where.minecraft_la: Minecraft Launcher: Installations > ... > Edit > More Options > JVM Arguments.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.where.curseforge: CurseForge: Settings > Minecraft > Java Settings > Additional Arguments.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.where.modrinth: Modrinth App: Instance > Settings > Java and memory > Java arguments.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.where.prism: Prism Launcher: Instance > Edit > Settings > Java > JVM arguments.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.where.multimc: MultiMC: Instance > Edit > Settings > Java > JVM arguments.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.where.unknown: In your launcher's settings for this game, find "JVM arguments" or "Java arguments".
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.args.note: This warning goes away by itself once it's working.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.explain.title: What the Argument Does
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.explain.shortcut: On newer Intel and AMD processors, Java uses a fast shortcut to read Base64, a kind of text Minecraft uses for things like skins and server icons. The bug is in that shortcut.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.explain.does: The argument switches the shortcut off, so Java reads Base64 the normal, safe way. Everything else in Java stays the same.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.explain.cost: Reading Base64 gets a little slower, but Minecraft reads so little of it that you won't notice.
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.confirm.title: Play Without the Fix?
gui.mcjavasafetycheck.confirm.body: Until you update Java or add the argument, a hostile multiplayer server could crash your game or run code on your computer.
